text:
A cube is placed inside an electric field, $\vec{E}=150y^{2}\hat{j}$. The side of the cube is 0.5 m and is placed in the field as shown in the given figure. The charge inside the cube is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the side of the cube, s = 0.5 m

Electric field, $E = 150 y^{2}\hat{j}$

The direction of electric field is as shown in the below figure,

 
[IMG]
 
At bottom surface, y = 0

As we know that, the expression of electric flux,

$𝜙$ = E . A cos$θ$

Here, E is the electric field passing through the cube and A is the surface area of the cube.

Substituting the values in the above equations, we get

$𝜙$ $= 150y^{2} . (0.5$ $\times$ 0.5) $\times$ cos180${}^{\circ }$

$= 150(0)^{2} . (0.25)$ $\times$ ($-$1) = 0

Hence, the electric flux is zero at the bottom surface.

At the top surface, y = 0.5 m

Electric field, $E = 150 y^{2}\hat{j}$ $= 150(0.5)^{2} = 37.5 N/C$

Electric flux at the top surface,

$𝜙$ = E . A cos$θ$

= (37.5) . (0.5 $\times$ 0.5) cos0${}^{\circ }$

$= 9.375 N / C - m^{2}$

By using the Gauss's law, $𝜙=\frac{Q_{in}}{ε_{0}}$

Here, $Q_{$in} = net charge enclosed in the cube and $ε_{0}$ = permittivity of the free space.

Substituting the values in the above equation, we get

$9.375=\frac{Q_{in}}{8.85\times 10^{-12}}$

$Q_{$in} = 8.3 $\times$ $10^{-11} C$

The charge inside the cube is 8.3 $\times$ $10^{-11} C$.

text:
A square loop of side 20 cm and resistance 1$\Omega$ is moved towards right with a constant speed $v_{0}$. The right arm of the loop is in a uniform magnetic field of 5T. The field is perpendicular to the plane of the loop and is going into it. The loop is connected to a network of resistors each of value 4$\Omega$. What should be the value of $v_{0}$ so that a steady current of 2 mA flows in the loop?


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to given circuit diagram, equivalent resistance between point P and Q.

$R_{PQ}=(4+4)||(4+4)$

$=\frac{8\times 8}{8+8}=4\Omega$

The equivalent circuit can be drawn as,

 
[IMG]
 
Equivalent resistance, $R_{eq} = 4 + 1 = 5$ $\Omega$

Magnetic field, B = 5T

The side of the square loop, l = 20 cm = 0.20 m

The steady value of the current, I = 2 mA = 2 $\times$ $10^{-3} A$

Induced emf, $e = Bv_{0}l$

Induced current, $I = e / R_{eq}$

Substituting the values in the above equation, we get

$2\times 10^{-3}=\frac{5\times v_{0}\times 0.2}{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{0} = 10^{-2} m/s = 1 cm/s$

$\therefore$ The value of $v_{0} = 1 cm/s$, so that a steady current of 2 mA flows in the loop.

text:
The temperature of an ideal gas in 3-dimensions is 300 K. The corresponding de-Broglie wavelength of the electron approximately at 300 K, is :

[$m_{e} =$ mass of electron = 9 $\times$ $10^{-31} kg, h =$ Planck constant = 6.6 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js, k_{B} =$ Boltzmann constant = 1.38 $\times$ $10^{-23} JK^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, Planck's constant, h = 6.6 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js$

Boltzmann constant, $k_{B} = 1.38$ $\times$ $10^{-23} J/K$

Mass of an electron, $m_{e} = 9$ $\times$ $10^{-31} kg$

Temperature of an ideal gas, T = 300 K

As we know that, de-Broglie wavelength,

$λ=\frac{h}{mv}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$ .... (i)

Here, E is the kinetic energy,

$E=\frac{3K_{B}T}{2}$

Substituting value of E in Eq. (i), we get

$λ=\frac{h}{\sqrt{3mK_{B}T}}$

Substituting the given values in the above equation, we get

$λ=\frac{6.6\times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{3\times 9\times 10^{-31}\times 1.38\times 10^{-23}\times 300}}$

= 6.26 nm

$\therefore$ The corresponding de-Broglie wavelength of an electron approximately at 300 K is 6.26 nm.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: A body of mass 'm' dropped from a height 'h' reaches the ground with a speed of 0.8$\sqrt{gh}$. The value of work done by the air-friction is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the mass of the body = m

The height from which the body dropped = h

The speed of the body when reached the ground, $v_{f}=0.8\sqrt{gh}$

Initial velocity of the body, v = 0 m/s

Using the work-energy theorem,

Work done by gravity + Work done by air-friction = Final kinetic energy $-$ Initial kinetic energy.

$W_{mg}+W_{air-friction}=\frac{1}{2}mv_{f}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}mv_{i}^{2}$

Here, work done by gravity = mgh

$\Rightarrow mgh+W_{air-friction}=\frac{1}{2}m(0.8\sqrt{gh})^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m(0)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow W_{air-friction}=\frac{0.64mgh}{2}-mgh$

$\Rightarrow 0.32mgh-mgh=-0.68mgh$

The value of the work done by the air friction is $-$ 0.68 mgh.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: The ranges and heights for two projectiles projected with the same initial velocity at angles 42${}^{\circ }$ and 48${}^{\circ }$ with the horizontal are $R_{1}, R_{2}$ and $H_{1}, H_{2}$ respectively. Choose the correct option :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here, two projectiles are projected at angles 42${}^{\circ }$ and 48${}^{\circ }$ with same initial velocity.

As we know the expression of range of projectile, 

Range $=\frac{u^{2}\sin 2θ}{g}$

At $θ_{1}$ = 42${}^{\circ }$,

Range, $R_{1}=\frac{u^{2}\sin 2(42)^{\circ }}{g}=\frac{0.99u^{2}}{g}$

At $θ_{2}$ = 48${}^{\circ }$ 

Range, $R_{2}=\frac{u^{2}\sin 2(48)^{\circ }}{g}=\frac{0.99u^{2}}{g}$

The range of the projectile is same for the two projectiles.

Therefore, $R_{1} = R_{2}$

Now, as we know the expression of height of the projectile,

$H_{\max }=\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}θ}{2g}$

At 42${}^{\circ }$, $H_{\max }=H_{1}=\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}42^{\circ }}{2g}=\frac{0.448u^{2}}{2g}$

At 48${}^{\circ }$, $H_{\max }=H_{2}=\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}48^{\circ }}{2g}=\frac{0.552u^{2}}{2g}$

Higher the value of $θ$ higher the value of maximum height. Therefore, $H_{1} < H_{2}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: Due to cold weather a 1 m water pipe of cross-sectional area $1 cm^{2}$ is filled with ice at $-$10${}^{\circ }$C. Resistive heating is used to melt the ice. Current of 0.5A is passed through 4 k$\Omega$ resistance. Assuming that all the heat produced is used for melting, what is the minimum time required? (Given latent heat of fusion for water/ice = 3.33 $\times$ $10^{5} J kg^{-1}$, specific heat of ice = 2 $\times$ $10^{3} J kg^{-1}$ and density of ice $= 10^{3} kg/m^{3})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the length of the water pipe, L = 1 m

The cross-sectional area of the water pipe, $A = 1 cm^{2} = 10^{-4} m^{2}$

The temperature of the ice = $-$ 10${}^{\circ }$C

Current passing in the conductor, I = 0.5 A

Resistance of the conductor, R = 4 k$\Omega$

The latent heat of fusion for ice, $L_{f} = 3.33$ $\times$ $10^{5} J/kg$

The density of the ice, $d = 1000 kg/m^{3}$

The specific heat of the ice, $c_{p$, ice}  = 2 $\times$ $10^{3} J/kg$

Heat required to melt the ice at $-$10${}^{\circ }$C to 0${}^{\circ }$C

$Q = mc_{p}\Delta T + mL_{f}$ $\Rightarrow$ Q = dVc$_{p}\Delta$T + dVL$_{f}$

= 1000 $\times$ $10^{-4}$ $\times$ 2 $\times$ $10^{3}$ $\times$ (10) + 1000 $\times$ $10^{-4}$ $\times$ 3.33 $\times$ $10^{5} (\because$ V = A $\times$ L)

= 35300 J

According to the Joule's law of heating,

$H = I^{2}Rt$

$\Rightarrow$ $35300 = (0.5)^{2}(4000) (t)$

$\Rightarrow$ t = 35.3 s

Thus, the minimum time required to melt the ice is 35.3 s.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: Two resistors $R_{1} = (4$ $\pm$ 0.8) $\Omega$ and $R_{2} = (4$ $\pm$ 0.4) $\Omega$ are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of their parallel combination will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, 

$R_{1} = (4$ $\pm$ 0.8) $\Omega$

$R_{2} = (4$ $\pm$ 0.4) $\Omega$

Equivalent resistance when the resistors are connected in parallel is given by

$\frac{1}{R_{eq}}=\frac{1}{R_{1}}+\frac{1}{R_{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{R_{eq}}=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}$

$R_{eq}=2\Omega$

Now, $\frac{\Delta R_{eq}}{R_{eq}^{2}}=\frac{\Delta R_{1}}{R_{1}^{2}}+\frac{\Delta R_{2}}{R_{2}^{2}}$

Substituting the values in the above equation, we get

$\frac{\Delta R_{eq}}{4}=\frac{0.8}{16}+\frac{0.4}{16}\Rightarrow \Delta R_{eq}=0.3\Omega$

$\therefore$ The equivalent resistance in parallel combination is $R_{eq}=(2\pm 0.3)\Omega$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: A glass tumbler having inner depth of 17.5 cm is kept on a table. A student starts pouring water ($μ$ = 4/3) into it while looking at the surface of water from the above. When he feels that the tumbler is half filled, he stops pouring water. Up to what height, the tumbler is actually filled?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the actual height of water be $h$. Seen from above, the bottom of the tumbler appears raised, and the apparent depth of the water is

$\frac{h}{μ}=\frac{3h}{4}$

The water surface is seen at its true position, $17.5-h$ below the rim, so the tumbler appears half filled when the apparent water depth equals the depth of the empty part:

$\frac{3h}{4}=17.5-h\Rightarrow \frac{7h}{4}=17.5\Rightarrow h=10\text{cm}$

Setting the apparent depth equal to $8.75\text{cm}$ ignores that the whole tumbler, not just the water, looks shallower.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text:
A mass of 5 kg is connected to a spring. The potential energy curve of the simple harmonic motion executed by the system is shown in the figure. A simple pendulum of length 4 m has the same period of oscillation as the spring system. What is the value of acceleration due to gravity on the planet where these experiments are performed?

 
[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the potential energy curve,

$U_{\max }=\frac{1}{2}kA^{2}$

$10=\frac{1}{2}k(2)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ k = 5 N/m

The length of the simple pendulum, L = 4 m

Time period of spring,

$T=2π\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}$

Time period of simple pendulum,

$T=2π\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$

The time period of simple pendulum is same as the time period of the spring oscillation.

$\Rightarrow$ $2π\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$ = $2π\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}$

Substituting the values in the above equations, we get

$2π\sqrt{\frac{4}{g}}$ = $2π\sqrt{\frac{5}{5}}$

$g = 4m/s^{2}$

$\therefore$ The acceleration due to the gravity on the planet is $4 m/s^{2}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: A capacitor is connected to a 20 V battery through a resistance of 10$\Omega$. It is found that the potential difference across the capacitor rises to 2 V in 1 $μ$s. The capacitance of the capacitor is $__________$ $μ$F. Given : $\ln \left (\frac{10}{9}\right )=0.105$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the peak voltage of the battery, $V_{0} = 20V$

The voltage of the battery, V = 2V

Time, t = 1 $μ$s = 1 $\times$ $10^{-6}s$

Resistance of the capacitor, R = 10 $\Omega$

As we know that, 

$V = V_{0}(1$ $-$ $e^{-t/RC})$

Substituting the values in the above equation, we get

2 = 20(1 $-$ $e^{-t/RC})$

$\Rightarrow \frac{t}{RC}=\ln \left (\frac{10}{9}\right )$

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{t}{R\ln (10/9)}=\frac{10^{-6}}{10\times \ln (10/9)}=0.95$ $μ$F

$\therefore$ The capacitance of the capacitor is 0.95 $μ$F.

text:
Four particles each of mass M, move along a circle of radius R under the action of their mutual gravitational attraction as shown in figure. The speed of each particle is :

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let us consider the gravitational force acting on each mass M by adjacent particles be F.

and the gravitational force acting on each mass M diagonally be $F_{1}$.


[IMG]

$F_{net}=\frac{MV^{2}}{R}$

Along the centre of circle,

$\sqrt{2}F+F_{1}=\frac{MV^{2}}{R}$

$\sqrt{2}\frac{GMM}{\left (\sqrt{2}R\right )^{2}}+\frac{GMM}{(2R)^{2}}=\frac{MV^{2}}{R}$

$\frac{GM}{R}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{4}\right )=V^{2}$

$\frac{GM}{R}\left (\frac{4+\sqrt{2}}{4\sqrt{2}}\right )=V^{2}$

$V=\sqrt{\frac{GM\left (4+\sqrt{2}\right )}{R4\sqrt{2}}}$

$V=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{GM\left (2\sqrt{2}+1\right )}{R}}$

text:
Electric field of plane electromagnetic wave propagating through a non-magnetic medium is given by 

E = 20cos(2 $\times$ $10^{10} t$ $-$ 200x) V/m. The dielectric constant of the medium is equal to : (Take $μ_{r}$ = 1)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, electric field,

E = 20 cos(2 $\times$ $10^{10}t$ $-$ 200 x) V/m

Comparing with the standard equation,

$E = E_{0} \cos (ω$t $-$ kx) V/m, we get

Wave constant, k = 200

Angular frequency, $ω$ = 2 $\times$ $10^{10}$ rad/s

Speed of the wave, $v=\frac{ω}{k}=\frac{2\times 10^{10}}{200}=10^{8}$ m/s

Refractive index, $μ=\frac{c}{v}=\frac{3\times 10^{8}}{10^{8}}=3$

As we know the relation between the refractive index and dielectric constant,

$μ=\sqrt{ε_{r}μ_{r}}$

Substituting the value in the above equations, we get

$3=\sqrt{ε_{r}(1)}$

$ε_{r}=9$

Thus, the dielectric constant of the medium is 9.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text:
There are two infinitely long straight current carrying conductors and they are held at right angles to each other so that their common ends meet at the origin as shown in the figure given below. The ratio of current in both conductor is 1 : 1. The magnetic field at point P is $____________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

$B_{$due to wire (1)} = $\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πy}[\sin 90+\sin θ_{1}]$

$=\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\frac{I}{y}\left (1+\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}\right )$ ....(1)

$B_{$due to wire (2)} = $\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\frac{I}{x}(\sin 90^{\circ }+\sin θ_{2})$

$=\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\frac{I}{x}\left (1+\frac{y}{\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}\right )$ ....(2)

Total magnetic field

$B=B_{1}+B_{2}$

$B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4π}\left [\frac{1}{y}+\frac{x}{y\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}+\frac{1}{x}+\frac{y}{x\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}\right ]$

$B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4π}\left [\frac{x+y}{xy}+\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}}{xy\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}\right ]$

$B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4π}\left [\frac{x+y}{xy}+\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}{xy}\right ]$

$B=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4πxy}\left [\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}+(x+y)\right ]$

Option (1)

text: The temperature of 3.00 mol of an ideal diatomic gas is increased by 40.0${}^{\circ }$C without changing the pressure of the gas. The molecules in the gas rotate but do not oscillate. If the ratio of change in internal energy of the gas to the amount of workdone by the gas is $\frac{x}{10}$. Then the value of x (round off to the nearest integer) is $___________. ($Given R = 8.31 J mol$^{-1} K^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the number of diatomic moles, n = 3 mol

The increase in temperature of the diatomic mole, 

$\Delta$T = 40${}^{\circ }$C

Now, the degree of freedom

f = linear + rotational + no oscillation

f = 3 + 2 + 0 $\Rightarrow$ f = 5

Change in internal energy,

$\Delta U = nC_{v}\Delta$T .... (i)

where, $C_{v}=\frac{f}{2}R=\frac{5}{2}R$

Substituting the value in Eq. (i), we get

$\Delta U=\frac{5R}{2}nR\Delta T$

Now, work done by the gas for isobaric process,

$W=p\Delta V=nR\Delta T$

The ratio of the change in internal energy to the work done by the gas,

$\frac{\Delta U}{W}=\frac{\frac{5}{2}nR\Delta T}{nR\Delta T}$

$=\frac{\Delta U}{W}=\frac{5}{2}$

Multiply and divide the above equation with 5, we get

$\frac{\Delta U}{W}=\frac{5\times 5}{2\times 5}=\frac{25}{10}$

Comparing with given equation, $\frac{\Delta U}{W}=\frac{x}{10}$

The value of the x = 25.

text: The width of one of the two slits in a Young's double slit experiment is three times the other slit. If the amplitude of the light coming from a slit is proportional to the slit-width, the ratio of minimum to maximum intensity in the interference pattern is x : 4 where x is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $b_{1} = 3b_{2}$

Here, $b_{1} =$ width of the one of the two slit and $b_{2} =$ width of the other slit.

As we know that,

Intensity, I $\propto$ (Amplitude$)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=\left (\frac{b_{1}}{b_{2}}\right )^{2}\Rightarrow \frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=\left (\frac{3b_{2}}{b_{2}}\right )^{2}$

$I_{1}=9I_{2}$

As we know, the ratio of the minimum intensity to the maximum intensity in the interference pattern,

$\frac{I_{\min }}{I_{\max }}=\left (\frac{\sqrt{I_{1}}-\sqrt{I_{2}}}{\sqrt{I_{1}}+\sqrt{I_{2}}}\right )^{2}$

Substituting the values in the above equations, we get

$\frac{I_{\min }}{I_{\max }}=\frac{(\sqrt{9I_{2}}-\sqrt{I_{2}})^{2}}{(\sqrt{9I_{2}}+\sqrt{I_{2}})^{2}}=\left (\frac{3-1}{3+1}\right )^{2}$

$\frac{I_{\min }}{I_{\max }}=\frac{1}{4}$

Comparing with, $\frac{I_{\min }}{I_{\max }}=\frac{x}{4}$

The value of x = 1.

text: Two satellites revolve around a planet in coplanar circular orbits in anticlockwise direction. Their period of revolutions are 1 hour and 8 hours respectively. The radius of the orbit of nearer satellite is 2 $\times$ $10^{3} km$. The angular speed of the farther satellite as observed from the nearer satellite at the instant when both the satellites are closest is $\frac{π}{x}radh^{-1}$ where x is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

$T_{1} = 1$ hour

$\Rightarrow$ $ω_{1}$ = 2$π$ rad/hour

$T_{2} = 8$ hours

$\Rightarrow$ $ω_{2}$ = $\frac{π}{4}$ rad/hour

$R_{1} = 2$ $\times$ $10^{3} km$

As $T^{2}$ $\propto$ $R^{3}$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}\right )^{3}=\left (\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}=\left (\frac{8}{1}\right )^{2/3}=4\Rightarrow R_{2}=8\times 10^{3}$ km


[IMG]

$V_{1} =$ $ω_{1}R_{1} = 4π$ $\times$ $10^{3} km/h$

$V_{2} =$ $ω_{2}R_{2} = 2π$ $\times$ $10^{3} km/h$

Relative $ω$ = $\frac{V_{1}-V_{2}}{R_{2}-R_{1}}=\frac{2π\times 10^{3}}{6\times 10^{3}}$

$=\frac{π}{3}$ rad/hour

x = 3

text: When a body slides down from rest along a smooth inclined plane making an angle of 30${}^{\circ }$ with the horizontal, it takes time T. When the same body slides down from the rest along a rough inclined plane making the same angle and through the same distance, it takes time $α$T, where $α$ is a constant greater than 1. The co-efficient of friction between the body and the rough plane is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\left (\frac{α^{2}-1}{α^{2}}\right )$ where $x = __________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

On smooth incline

a = g sin30${}^{\circ }$

by S = ut + $\frac{1}{2}$at$^{2}$

S = $\frac{1}{2}\frac{g}{2}T^{2} =$ $\frac{g}{4}T^{2} ........ (i)$


[IMG]

For rough surface,

$ma=mg\sin 30^{\circ }-μmg\cos 30^{\circ }$

$a=g\sin 30^{\circ }-μg\cos 30^{\circ }$

Distance covered by the block on the rough surface in time $α$T,

$s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^{2}$

$s=0+\frac{1}{2}(g\sin 30^{\circ }-μg\cos 30^{\circ })t^{2}$

$s=\frac{g}{4}(1-\sqrt{3}μ)(αT)^{2}$ .... (ii)

Distance covered by the block is same for both the case,

$\Rightarrow \frac{g}{4}(1-\sqrt{3}μ)(αT)^{2}=\frac{g}{4}T^{2}$ [from Eq. (i) and Eq. (ii)]

$\Rightarrow 1-\sqrt{3}μ=\frac{1}{α^{2}}\Rightarrow μ=\left (\frac{α^{2}-1}{α^{2}}\right )\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Comparing with $μ=\left (\frac{α^{2}-1}{α^{2}}\right )\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$

The value of the x = 3.

text: The average translational kinetic energy of $N_{2}$ gas molecules at .............${}^{\circ }$C becomes equal to the K.E. of an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 0.1 volt. (Given $k_{B} = 1.38$ $\times$ $10^{-23} J/K) ($Fill the nearest integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The average translational kinetic energy of a molecule comes only from its three translational degrees of freedom, so it equals $\dfrac{3}{2}k_{B}T$ for every gas. The two rotational degrees of freedom of $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ add rotational energy, not translational energy.

An electron accelerated from rest through $V=0.1\text{V}$ gains kinetic energy

$eV=1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 0.1=1.6\times 10^{-20}\text{J}$

Equating the two energies,

$\dfrac{3}{2}k_{B}T=eV\Rightarrow T=\dfrac{2\times 1.6\times 10^{-20}}{3\times 1.38\times 10^{-23}}\approx 773\text{K}$

In degree Celsius, $t=773-273=500{}^{\circ }\text{C}$.

Hence, the answer is 500.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: A uniform heating wire of resistance 36$\Omega$ is connected across a potential difference of 240 V. The wire is then cut into half and potential difference of 240V is applied across each half separately. The ratio of power dissipation in first case to the total power dissipation in the second case would be 1 : x, where x is $____________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For Case I,

The potential difference of the uniform wire, V = 240 V

The resistance of the uniform wire, $R_{1} = 36$ $\Omega$

The power dissipation in the first case,

$P_{1}=\frac{V^{2}}{R_{1}}=\frac{(240)^{2}}{36}$

For Case II,

The resistance of each half, $R_{2}=\frac{R_{1}}{2}=\frac{36}{2}=18\Omega$

$P_{2}=\frac{V^{2}}{R_{2}}+\frac{V^{2}}{R_{2}}=\frac{(240)^{2}}{18}+\frac{(240)^{2}}{18}=\frac{(240)^{2}}{9}$

Thus, the ratio of the total power dissipation in the first case to the second case

$\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\frac{(240)^{2}/36}{(240)^{2}/9}\Rightarrow \frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\frac{1}{4}$

Comparing with, $\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\frac{1}{x}$

The value of the x = 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: A steel rod with y = 2.0 $\times$ $10^{11} Nm^{-2}$ and $α$ $= 10^{-5}$ ${}^{\circ }C^{-1}$ of length 4 m and area of cross-section $10 cm^{2}$ is heated from 0${}^{\circ }$C to 400${}^{\circ }$C without being allowed to extend. The tension produced in the rod is x $\times$ $10^{5} N$ where the value of x is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the Young's modulus of the steel rod, Y = 2 $\times$ $10^{11} Pa$

Thermal coefficient of the steel rod, $α$ $= 10^{-5}{}^{\circ }$C

The length of the steel rod, l = 4 m

The area of the cross-section, $A = 10 cm^{2}$

The temperature difference, $\Delta$T = 400${}^{\circ }$C

As we know that,

Thermal strain = $α$ $\Delta$T

Using the Hooke's law

Young's modulus (Y) = $\frac{Thermalstress}{Thermalstrain}=\frac{F/A}{α\Delta T}$

Thermal stress, $F=YAα\Delta T$

Substitute the values in the above equation, we get

$F=2\times 10^{11}\times 10\times 10^{-4}\times 10^{-5}\times (400)$

$=8\times 10^{5}N$

Comparing with, $F=x\times 10^{5}N$

The value of the x = 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: A 2 kg steel rod of length 0.6 m is clamped on a table vertically at its lower end and is free to rotate in vertical plane. The upper end is pushed so that the rod falls under gravity, ignoring the friction due to clamping at its lower end, the speed of the free end of rod when it passes through its lowest position is $____________ ms^{-1}. ($Take $g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The rod ($m=2\text{kg}$, $l=0.6\text{m}$) turns about its clamped lower end in a vertical plane, from standing vertically above the clamp to hanging vertically below it.


[IMG]

The centre of mass starts $\dfrac{l}{2}$ above the clamp and ends $\dfrac{l}{2}$ below it, so it falls through a height $l$.

The moment of inertia of the rod about its end is $I=\dfrac{ml^{2}}{3}$. The rod starts essentially from rest and the clamp is frictionless, so

$mgl=\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\dfrac{ml^{2}}{3}\right )ω^{2}\Rightarrow ω=\sqrt{\dfrac{6g}{l}}$

The free end moves on a circle of radius $l$:

$v=ωl=\sqrt{6gl}=\sqrt{6\times 10\times 0.6}=6\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 6.

text: An engine is attached to a wagon through a shock absorber of length 1.5 m. The system with a total mass of 40,000 kg is moving with a speed of 72 kmh$^{-1}$ when the brakes are applied to bring it to rest. In the process of the system being brought to rest, the spring of the shock absorber gets compressed by 1.0 m. If 90% of energy of the wagon is lost due to friction, the spring constant is $____________$ $\times$ $10^{5} N/m$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, the length of the shock absorber, l = 1.5 m

The total mass of the system, M = 40000 kg

The speed of the wagon, v = 72 km/h

When brakes are applied, the final velocity, $v_{f} = 0$

The compressed spring of the shock absorber, x = 1 m

Applying the work-energy theorem,

Work done by the system = Change in kinetic energy

$W=\Delta KE$

$W_{friction}+W_{spring}=\frac{1}{2}mv_{f}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}mv_{i}^{2}$

$-\frac{90}{100}\left (\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\right )+W_{spring}=0-\frac{1}{2}mv_{i}^{2}$ ($\because$ 90% energy lost due to friction)

$W_{spring}=-\frac{10}{100}\times \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$-\frac{1}{2}kx^{2}=-\frac{1}{20}mv^{2}$

$k=\frac{mv^{2}}{10\times x^{2}}$

Substituting the values in the above equation, we get

$k=\frac{40000\times \left (72\times \frac{5}{18}\right )^{2}}{10(1)^{2}}$

= 16 $\times$ $10^{5} N/m$

Comparing the spring constant, k = x $\times$ $10^{5}$

The value of the x = 16.
